## v0.89.3: v0.89.3

**Published**: 2026-11-04

### Patch Changes

- Mermaid and Excalidraw tabs no longer add .md to the file name in their hover tooltip and screen reader label, and the tab menu's Rename, Copy path and Hide this file actions now use the actual file.
- Mermaid diagrams open in source mode now keep their cursor and scroll position when you switch to another tab and back.

## v0.89.2: v0.89.2

**Published**: 2026-11-02

### Patch Changes

- In the default light theme, the keyboard focus ring on thread history rows now stands out at least 3:1 against the sidebar.
- Switching back to a recently viewed tab now shows the Mermaid diagrams it already rendered, instead of pausing to render them again.
- Color themes now reach the editor: document text, code block titles, find highlights, table cell selection, unresolved links, skill references, comment highlights, and Timeline and agent diffs take the active theme's colors, and skill references in the default theme now use the link color.
- While you scroll a long table, the pinned header row no longer shows slivers of body text at its top and bottom edges.
- The graph view, its legend and hover cards, and skill preview cards now draw with the active color theme's colors, and an open graph recolors when the theme changes. Graph clusters now take the theme's eight accent colors, so cluster colors repeat sooner than before.
- Typing into a new page no longer loses keystrokes or focus when the page is first saved.
- Color themes now shift a faint secondary text color until it reads at 4.5:1 on page, card, menu and sidebar backgrounds and on highlighted rows in the command palette and similar pickers, where the label color also reaches 4.5:1, most visibly in Catppuccin Latte, Frappé and Solarized.
- Long file-type labels, such as TRANSCRIPT, no longer spill past the left edge of the command palette and file suggestions. Labels now show only for extensions of four letters or fewer, so `.jsonl` and other five-letter extensions no longer show one.
- Color themes reach source-mode and property links, comment and Help menu highlights, table handles, file tree icons and guides, agent panel text, Navigator project names and preview scrollbars. Links and hovered Help menu rows stay readable in every theme, and default-theme source-mode and property links use the link color.

## v0.89.1: v0.89.1

**Published**: 2026-10-30

### Patch Changes

- In the default light theme, secondary gray text is slightly darker, so it now meets the 4.5:1 text contrast standard on the standard light gray background, such as in gray badges.
- In the default light and dark themes, the keyboard focus ring most controls share now stands out at least 3:1 against the surface around it, so the focused control is easier to find. Selection outlines in the same color, such as on selected images and blocks, are stronger too.

## v0.88.12: v0.88.12

**Published**: 2026-10-29

### Patch Changes

- Reduce disk writes from backlink caching during sustained editing.
- Documents with very large or deeply nested MDX component props stay editable instead of failing to render.
- Building the Claude Cowork skill no longer crashes the server or `ok cowork` when the system file opener is missing, such as Linux without `xdg-open`. `ok cowork` says the file was built but not opened.
- Opening a Markdown file from Finder or Open With now opens that file in its project's window when the window is already open or still loading, instead of only bringing the window to the front.
- A table's frozen header row no longer sticks partway down the page after the window is resized.
- Hidden editor choices now survive quitting and relaunching a project window.
- Honor the configured Git default branch when creating a project repository.
- Fix false broken-link warnings from agent writes and edits for existing source files in directories such as Applications, vendor, build, and dist.
- On Windows, opening a file on a different drive no longer stops the project from starting with a "path should be a `path.relative()`d string" error.
- An edit another app makes to a new page moments after OpenKnowledge first saves it now reaches the open page, and a new `.mdx` file opened before OpenKnowledge has listed it now loads its content instead of an empty page.
- Agent installs such as OpenCode no longer fail on slower connections after two minutes. Downloads resume after a dropped or stalled connection, and give up only when repeated attempts make no progress.
- A share link that needs a branch switch now shows its branch-switch prompt when the project's window is still loading, instead of being dropped.
- Skill creation, import, refresh and rename now refuse out-of-scope or private-state destinations and linked `SKILL.md` files. Supporting-file changes reject links on the affected path, while refresh checks every file it would write or remove; in-scope linked skill roots remain supported.
- Wait for the desktop watchdog worker to finish inspector teardown before starting the next session.
- Stop oversized website skill downloads early and cancel the remaining downloads when a bundle exceeds its size limits.
- Large projects list documents and pages faster, and the server uses about 40 MB less memory.

## v0.88.10: v0.88.10

**Published**: 2026-10-28

### Patch Changes

- Pasted and dropped files now go to a folder per document by default, `./{{filename}}.assets`, and the attachment setting is one path field. Update collaborators first: 0.86.18 and earlier reject `/folder` values.
- Ensure cloning into an existing OpenKnowledge project initializes the new checkout without changing the enclosing project's files.
- Screen readers now announce a name for each source and code editor, such as Markdown source mode, text files and Mermaid diagram source.
- Resolve explicit `deinit` paths relative to the command's working directory so ancestor project detection cannot remove a different project's setup.
- OpenKnowledge Desktop now builds with the stable electron-vite 6.0.0 release instead of a beta, with no change to the app itself.
- An email link followed directly by an underscore, such as `a@b.com` before `_case`, now saves in a form that opens again as the same link. Before, the file opened as a link to a different address.
- An empty bullet, numbered item, heading or quote made by typing its marker now saves as that block, not as an escaped literal such as `\*`.
- Git operations that OpenKnowledge authenticates start faster: its credential helper now answers about six times faster, and git no longer prints "unknown command 'store'" or "unknown command 'erase'" after each fetch or push.
- Pasted formatted text and links now stay in the bullet, heading, quote or paragraph at the cursor instead of moving to a new paragraph outside it. A link pasted right next to a word stays a link.
- Slash-menu and component descriptions now describe each feature directly instead of comparing it to other apps.
- Typing right after Enter keeps the caret after the first character, so a fast `* ` or `- ` turns into a bullet instead of landing before the marker.
- Keep `ok clone --json` and `ok init --json` output parseable by sending initialization diagnostics to stderr.
- Opening a file or skill from the sidebar keeps it in the preview tab instead of sometimes pinning it.
- Contributor typechecks now run on `tsrs`, a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler. On Windows or an Intel Mac, set `TSRS_BINARY` first, as the [contributing guide](https://github.com/inkeep/open-knowledge/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#toolchain) explains.

Delta since previous beta ([v0.88.6-beta.1](https://github.com/inkeep/open-knowledge/releases/tag/v0.88.6-beta.1)) — 3 new changesets.

### Patch Changes

## v0.88.6-beta.1: v0.88.6-beta.1

**Published**: 2026-10-27

Delta since previous beta ([v0.88.6-beta.0](https://github.com/inkeep/open-knowledge/releases/tag/v0.88.6-beta.0)) — 6 new changesets.

Proved by internal Inertia run [40439444675](https://github.com/inkeep/agents-private/actions/runs/40439444675) at agents-private commit `a44f82e9812932faf3b6048f7ca6268b142cb587`.

### Patch Changes

- Pasted and dropped files now go to a folder per document by default, `./{{filename}}.assets`, and the attachment setting is one path field. Update collaborators first: 0.86.18 and earlier reject `/folder` values.

- Pasted formatted text and links now stay in the bullet, heading, quote or paragraph at the cursor instead of moving to a new paragraph outside it. A link pasted right next to a word stays a link.

- Opening a file or skill from the sidebar keeps it in the preview tab instead of sometimes pinning it.

- Contributor typechecks now run on `tsrs`, a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler. On Windows or an Intel Mac, set `TSRS_BINARY` first, as the [contributing guide](https://github.com/inkeep/open-knowledge/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#toolchain) explains.

- Typing right after Enter keeps the caret after the first character, so a fast `* ` or `- ` turns into a bullet instead of landing before the marker.

- OpenKnowledge Desktop now builds with the stable electron-vite 6.0.0 release instead of a beta, with no change to the app itself.

## v0.88.3: v0.88.3

**Published**: 2026-10-26

### Patch Changes

- Archived chats now reopen from Chat history without an app reload, and failed history loads show a helpful error.
- Let large MCP audit and project-wide lint scans run beyond 30 seconds. Client timeouts still apply, with a 120-second limit for `ok mcp --port` and Node's 300-second response-header deadline; narrow the scan path when needed.
- Servers now finish starting before idle shutdown can stop them.
- Reject `__proto__` fields in frontmatter patches and merged document writes before saving, preventing silent data loss.
- Keep bullet markers visible when normal and checkbox items share a list.
- Bug reports now include the newest macOS update-installer logs, the machine's memory pressure before an unexpected exit, and which signal stopped the local server.
- Keep preview tabs marked as previews when session restoration finishes after a file is opened.
- Keep server logs, diagnostic spans, and startup errors outside project folders to avoid cloud-file sync churn. Support bundles still collect diagnostics left by older versions.
- Stopping a server now keeps stopping its other file watchers when one of them fails to stop.
- Closing a slide presentation after its server has already exited no longer sends a stop signal to that server's old process ID.
- A project now opens after a restart even when its old server's process ID was reused by a process OpenKnowledge cannot inspect, such as a protected Windows service.
- Release watcher subscriptions that finish initializing after server shutdown begins.
- Fix inherited templates missing from nested folders on Windows.

## v0.88.2: v0.88.2

**Published**: 2026-10-23

### Patch Changes

- Move docked chat history to either side of the conversation: right-click an empty part of the Agents tab strip, or search the command palette. The Chat history button moves to the same side, and the desktop app keeps the choice for every project.
- Pressing Escape in the Properties panel of a component that holds content, such as a Callout you just inserted, now returns focus to the document with the component still selected, so undo and typing work right away.
- Changing the properties of a component that is not inside another component now rewrites only its opening tag, unless you also edited its content. An unindented body no longer gains an indent, and changing a property back restores the original text.
- The default dark theme now layers surfaces the way light mode does: the window background is darkest, sidebars sit a step above it, documents are lighter still, and menus lighter again. Panels also get a thin edge in dark mode.
- Server shutdown now waits, up to a time limit, for backlink and tag cache writes to finish, so removing a project folder right after stopping its server no longer races those writes.
- Closing an agent chat before sending it a message now also removes that chat's browser files, as deleting a chat already did.
- Swap the file sidebar and the document panel to put your files on the right: right-click an empty part of the editor's tab row, or search the command palette. Each sidebar's show and hide button moves with it, and the desktop app keeps the choice for every project.
- A new image URL entered in the image's Properties panel is now saved, instead of the original relative path.
- In narrow windows, the Editor, Agents and Terminal buttons in the header now look like one switcher, with the panel you see raised.
- `{{date}}` in templates now fills in today's date in the time zone of the computer running OpenKnowledge instead of UTC, and new date properties default to your local date.

## v0.88.0: v0.88.0

**Published**: 2026-10-22

### Minor Changes

- Agent writes to Markdown documents, templates and project skills report `outcome`, `saved` and `nextStep`. `agent-write`, `agent-write-md`, `agent-patch` and `frontmatter-patch` answer 409 `both-kept` or 503 `save-held` where they answered 200: those writes landed, so do not retry. `retryWhen` and warning-level `nextStep` are deprecated.

### Patch Changes

- Unsaved edits to Mermaid, Excalidraw, text and settings files and to global and external skills are no longer lost to an outside change: the version set aside goes to history, or to a backup folder when history is unavailable, with a notice saying where.
- After a connection to its server drops, for example when the server restarts, OpenKnowledge no longer lets connections it has since replaced or closed reconnect in the background.

## v0.87.9: v0.87.9

**Published**: 2026-10-22

### Patch Changes

- Drag a panel by an empty part of its tab strip onto another panel's edge to dock it there, or onto its middle to swap the two. In the desktop app those tab strips no longer move the window; drag the header at the top of the window instead.
- The editor, Agents panel and terminal now split the window by proportion, and each project remembers its own arrangement. Panes no longer close when dragged small or when another one opens; hide them with the header buttons.
- Moving or renaming an open document outside OpenKnowledge now keeps it open under its new name with your unsaved typing. If its file is deleted, your typing is saved to history first. Switching git branches merges unsaved typing with the new branch instead of replacing it.
- A page that doesn't exist yet now shows "Start writing to create this page" until you type.

## v0.87.8: v0.87.8

**Published**: 2026-10-22

### Patch Changes

- Saving a Markdown document in the app, by an agent, while idle or at quit now checks the file first and merges an outside edit instead of writing over it. Agent writes over a changed file are merged instead of refused with `urn:ok:error:disk-divergence`, which is retired.
- When OpenKnowledge keeps both versions of an edit, or saves an outside version to the timeline because it could not merge it, the document now shows a quiet notice saying so. Timeline entries for those cases now say which version they hold.
- Outside edits the file watcher misses now appear within seconds, or about two minutes on very large projects: OpenKnowledge re-checks the project on a timer, watches again after a watcher failure, and re-reads open documents when the window regains focus or reconnects. Large projects use less memory.

## v0.87.6-beta.0: v0.87.6-beta.0

**Published**: 2026-10-21

### Patch Changes

- Drag a panel by an empty part of its tab strip onto another panel's edge to dock it there, or onto its middle to swap the two. In the desktop app those tab strips no longer move the window; drag the header at the top of the window instead.

- The editor, Agents panel and terminal now split the window by proportion, and each project remembers its own arrangement. Panes no longer close when dragged small or when another one opens; hide them with the header buttons.

- Moving or renaming an open document outside OpenKnowledge now keeps it open under its new name with your unsaved typing. If its file is deleted, your typing is saved to history first. Switching git branches merges unsaved typing with the new branch instead of replacing it.

- A page that doesn't exist yet now shows "Start writing to create this page" until you type.

## v0.87.0: v0.87.0

**Published**: 2026-10-19

### Minor Changes

- `ok start` and `ok clean` now treat a server lock as stale once another program reuses its process ID, and `ok stop` and the desktop app no longer signal that program. `ok stop` exits `1` if it cannot confirm the process; stop 0.25.0-or-earlier servers yourself, then restart them.

### Patch Changes

- OpenKnowledge Beta now shows one Beta label in the window header instead of two.
- OpenKnowledge Desktop's editor, note, navigator and terminal windows now apply a Content-Security-Policy and refuse to load local files from outside the app bundle, which stops scripts injected into the page from running.
- The Files sidebar now lists files while a large project is still indexing at startup, and its loading placeholder is visible on every color theme.
- OpenKnowledge no longer leaves stuck `zsh` processes behind when it checks your login shell's PATH.
- Cancelling a Mermaid label edit with Escape now restores the label exactly as the diagram showed it. Before, the editor read the label's source text as HTML, which skipped Mermaid's sanitizer.
- A bug report started from the toolbar's **?** menu no longer captures that button's "Resources" tooltip in its screenshot. The report shortcut still captures the command palette or any menu that is open.
- Opening a saved theme's editor in Settings, from its edit button or from Create & edit, now scrolls the editor into view and moves focus to it, without animation when reduced motion is on.
- Dismissing the "Name your theme" dialog in Settings now returns focus to the Create new theme tile.
- Typing a search in the command palette now selects the top result, so pressing Enter runs it without first pressing the down arrow.
- Command palette searches now list commands whose names match before commands that match only a related term, and Enter runs the top row. Typing "check" leads with **Check for updates** rather than **Switch worktree**.
- Skill install confirmations now open in an app dialog instead of the system prompt, a failed agent restart is reported in the agent pane instead of a toast, and retry buttons read "Try again".
- Selecting the Editor while an empty Agents panel is opening no longer moves focus back to Agents.
- Preserve the editor's viewport and caret when switching to Agents and back in a narrow window, and prevent position resets when navigating or typing immediately after switching editor modes or jumping to source.
- Keep document navigation responsive when reopening a large document by avoiding repeated statistics and wiki-link resolution work.
- Agent conversations now open the Agents panel even when the panel finishes loading after the conversation starts.
- Stop OpenKnowledge's saved version history from growing without bound when your project's `.git` resolves to a directory inside the project, such as a `.git.nosync` symlink or a separate git directory. That directory is now kept out of every new version.
- Status colors across the app, including update notices, banners, badges and agent thread warnings, now come from the active theme's palette, including custom themes, instead of fixed greens, ambers, reds and blues. Palette colors too faint to read are adjusted just enough to stay legible.

<!-- ok-notes-source: stable-tag-tree -->

## v0.86.19: v0.86.19

**Published**: 2026-10-16

### Patch Changes

- Graph view tooltips now show document titles and link URLs as plain text, even when they contain HTML tags.
- Translation catalogs are now compiled when the app is built, so contributors commit only the `.po` files.

## v0.86.18: v0.86.18

**Published**: 2026-10-15

### Patch Changes

- OpenKnowledge Beta now names `ok-beta` and `~/.ok-beta` in its remaining setup, diagnostics, sign-in, embeddings and connection messages, and the bundled skills note the Beta command alongside Stable's.
- OpenKnowledge Beta now names `ok-beta`, not `ok`, in its server-not-running and stuck-server hints, PATH setup copy, CLI help and the built-in terminal's Claude approval, and names `~/.ok-beta/secrets.yml` for its search key.
- Opening or closing the agents panel, and typing a long question in the Ask AI box, are now faster on large documents.
- Default dark mode gives the app frame, sidebars, and editor distinct neutral shades, subtler file names and badges, and brighter header button hovers.
- The desktop app and dev server run from source now use their own `dev` channel, with separate home folder, credentials, MCP entry and link scheme, so they no longer share or take over an installed app's state and projects.
- The area behind the cards and app header is a step darker and follows your color theme, the cards cast a soft shadow with a gap at the sides and bottom, the desktop file list is now opaque, and resize grips appear only when you hover a divider.
- The editor, its file list and document side panel now sit in one card, with the terminal and chat in their own cards. The side panel button moved to the end of the tab bar, and dragging the chat or right terminal divider keeps the side panel's width.
- Update notices and the feedback card now float in the window's bottom-left corner, so they stay visible when the editor is hidden or the file list is collapsed.
- A new header across the top of project windows keeps back, forward, search, the project switcher, Share, sync, settings and resources in one fixed place. The editor footer now shows the current checkout: its project folder and its branch or worktree.
- Project windows can now hide the editor from a new Editor header button or View › Show/Hide Editor, letting chat and the terminal fill the window. Opening a document brings the editor back.
- Project and single-file windows now have Agents and Terminal buttons at the right of the header that show whether each panel is open and toggle it with one click. They replace the right-edge chat tab, its live-agent dot and the panels' collapse arrows.
- The `@` and `/` menus now open when typing with a Japanese input method: after an ideographic space, on full-width `＠` and `／`, and once the input method commits the character.
- Projects in one git repository whose folder names differ only in non-Latin letters, spaces or punctuation now keep separate version histories, and such skill files keep separate discarded-edit backups. A history two projects already shared stays with the project that created it; the other starts fresh.
- The Linux packages are now named after the app they install: `openknowledge` for Stable on deb and rpm, and `openknowledge-beta` for Beta. Existing installs update in place and keep their terminal commands.
- When the editor is too narrow for its split panes, it shows one pane at a time with an Editor pane selector, keeping each pane's tabs and reading position.
- Windows narrower than 48rem show one of Editor, Agents and Terminal at a time, chosen from the header, keep the others running, and return to your full layout when widened.
- When the file sidebar or document panel cannot fit beside the document, it opens as a full-editor cover with Back to editor and Hide, and choosing a destination in it reveals the document.
- Choosing the same document heading again now scrolls to its destination.
- Showing or hiding Files or the document panel now applies at every window width, so a sidebar you hid stays hidden when the window widens.
- Single-file windows now use the shared header and editor cards, with the document panel in the editor card.
- On macOS, the window buttons in a single-file window now sit centered in its top bar instead of below the middle.
- Links and heading anchors in Japanese, Hindi, Thai and other scripts whose marks change a letter keep those marks, so `[[ガラス]]` no longer opens a page named カラス. Links the editor saved earlier without the marks, such as `#カラス` for `## ガラス`, need the marks restored.
- Suggested links now find page mentions in Chinese, Japanese, Thai and other text written without spaces, and report the right position when the text contains characters such as `İ`.
- Converting a page to a template no longer overwrites an existing template with the same generated name; it picks the next free name such as `imported-template-2`. Importing under an explicit name that is already taken is refused.
- Keep terminal text readable after changing themes while the terminal is closed.
- Template names, doc paths in agent chat, typed or pasted links with non-Latin domains, and agent names in thread titles now work in any script, and shortened titles and previews no longer cut an emoji or character in half.
- Tags can now use any script, including Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Cyrillic and accented Latin, in front matter and inline `#tags`. Existing non-ASCII tags that were hidden now appear in the tag list. Letters written directly after an inline tag name, such as `#wip日本語`, now extend that tag.

- Converting a page to a template no longer overwrites an existing template with the same generated name; it picks the next free name such as `imported-template-2`. Importing under an explicit name that is already taken is refused.

## v0.86.12: v0.86.12

**Published**: 2026-10-13

### Patch Changes

- History and agent-change diffs now render images, callouts and other components instead of empty boxes.

- Agent edits made during a Git branch switch now wait up to 20 seconds for it to finish before applying. An edit whose save the switch drops within that wait returns a `branch-switched` error instead of reporting success.

- Changing a Codex chat's context window while its agent is still starting, or retrying a chat whose agent failed to start, no longer leaves a second agent running. The chat's first message is sent once when its context window changes during start.

- Show translated error messages when an imported color theme is invalid.

- Text sent to a running or newly staged agent terminal now shows control characters as labels such as `<control-0003>`, so they can no longer end a Codex session or act as keystrokes. When the agent supports bracketed paste, the text arrives as one paste, which may display collapsed.

## v0.86.0: v0.86.0

**Published**: 2026-10-12

### Minor Changes

- The desktop app can now stop updating itself: turn off **Download and install updates automatically** in Settings → About & updates. Check for updates still works. Dismissing the "ready to install" card now sticks, and a failing install stops asking after a few tries.

### Patch Changes

- On macOS the desktop app no longer offers a crash report after the system ended it to free memory that another app was using.
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge@0.84.1-beta.0
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-core@0.84.1-beta.0
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-server@0.84.1-beta.0

- Document, template, skill-body and Markdown bundle-file writes now reject unsupported control characters with actionable errors, including template writes from agents and the app. Stored bytes are not rewritten; existing templates, skills and Markdown bundle files must have these characters removed before full saves or edits.

- The desktop app download is smaller on every platform; the macOS disk image drops from about 347 MB to about 189 MB.

- Agent edits to a path with no document now fail with "No document at" and suggest the likely path, instead of "Text not found" or silently creating a file. Appending or prepending to a missing path now says it created a new document.

- History and agent-change diffs now resolve relative links and inline images against the document's folder, so links to existing pages beside it no longer show as broken.

- Open in default app now reveals folders, app bundles, extensionless files and links whose real file has a different extension in the file manager instead of opening them. More script and installer types, such as `.py`, `.tool` and `.cpl`, are blocked too.

- On Linux, opening OpenKnowledge while it is already running no longer prints a "sonic boom is not ready yet" error as the second launch exits.
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge@0.85.1-beta.0
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-core@0.85.1-beta.0
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-server@0.85.1-beta.0

- An agent thread's status line now says "Installing" rather than "Starting" while the agent is downloaded and installed ahead of launch.

- Bug reports now show when desktop startup is waiting on the "Git not found" dialog, and which button was chosen.

- On Windows the desktop app no longer offers a crash report after you installed OpenKnowledge again while it was running.

## v0.85.0: v0.85.0

**Published**: 2026-10-09

### Minor Changes

- The desktop app's Settings now has a searchable About & updates page with the installed version, a Check for updates button and release notes, and the Help popover shows the version with a Check for updates action.

- Links to files that exist but are excluded by .gitignore or .okignore now say so in the Problems pane, the Links panel, and agent write results, with the .okignore re-include hint, instead of claiming the file does not exist.

- Links, backlinks, and the Problems pane now match documents, files, and folders whose names differ only in Unicode normalization (NFC vs NFD), and such images and files now load on Linux too. In the editor, markdown asset links now match parent folder names case-sensitively; file names stay case-insensitive.

### Patch Changes

- Overlapping projects and previews now refuse to start rather than write the same files. Close overlapping previews before opening a project, restart existing servers after updating, and restart the parent after creating a nested project.

- Renaming or moving files no longer waits for version history to save before it completes, so moving many files in a row is faster.

- A crash while saving the link or tag index cache no longer leaves a damaged cache behind.

- `ok init` now names each user-global skill correctly in its summary and shows how to add starter content even with `--no-mcp`.

- Check for updates now tells you when this copy of OpenKnowledge can't update itself, instead of showing nothing.

- On Windows and Linux, closing the last project window now returns to the Project Navigator instead of quitting. To close the app, use File → Exit on Windows or File → Quit on Linux.

- Moving many files that git does not track yet, one after another, is faster, because a rename no longer asks git about each of those files separately.

- The desktop Help menu now includes About on Windows and Linux, plus links to the documentation and Discord.

- Settings → Git now names the GitHub host and account you are connected to, and says how to switch or sign out of a GitHub CLI account.

- Stop the app and browser tabs from rewriting the file list into their disk cache on every refresh, which could add up to hundreds of gigabytes of disk writes in busy projects.

- The empty editor's "From template" list now says when a very large knowledge base had too many folders to list every template, and shows its count as a minimum.

- Counting skill installs on skills.sh is now off by default. Turn it on in Settings → Preferences → Count skill installs publicly; a choice you already made is kept.

- When **Check for updates…** finds a new version but its download fails, the app now shows an error instead of staying silent, and "Checking for updates…" stays visible during the check, including in Settings.

- Settings no longer offers the Auto sync modes before it knows the project has a Git remote. Settings and the sync menu show the Shared default sync mode when you haven't picked your own, and Settings explains that the Shared default only reaches teammates when Config sharing is Shared.

- Crash reports now attach only the crash dump from the crash that prompted them. If that dump can't be added, the report says so instead of attaching a different one.

- Running `open-knowledge-beta open`, or opening a Markdown file from the Beta command line, now opens it in the OpenKnowledge Beta app.

- Skills Studio now says a skill is not added to any AI tool yet instead of claiming no AI tools were detected. The title-bar build label no longer looks clickable; it shows the app version on hover and keyboard focus and announces it to screen readers.

- OpenKnowledge now refuses to set up a project at the top of a drive, and the desktop app also refuses system folders. Open folder reports an error when the picker closes without a folder.

- Agent writes to a busy local project now answer as soon as they are saved, carrying a `link-check-deferred` warning when link checks were skipped. A write refused because the project is overloaded now says that nothing was saved, so it is safe to retry.

- First-launch setup no longer pre-selects connecting your AI tools, installing the discovery skill, or adding `ok` to your terminal; tick the ones you want. Its pointer to Settings now names the Agent connections pane.

- Full bug reports and `ok diagnose bundle` now include what the operating system recorded about the app being ended, such as memory-pressure or out-of-memory kills, hangs, and shutdowns and restarts, so unexplained exits can be diagnosed.

- Settings… in the project navigator now opens Settings with your preferences and hotkeys instead of the integrations dialog. Use Set up OpenKnowledge integrations… to connect AI tools.

- Deleting an empty bullet in unusually indented Markdown no longer brings the bullet back.

- The Help menu footer no longer cuts off "About & updates" or scrolls sideways when the version number is long.

- The server no longer stops responding for a minute or more after startup while it reads large installed skills, which made the first MCP call time out.

- The Settings close button now closes Settings on the first click after File → Settings or its shortcut was used while Settings was already open.
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge@0.84.1-beta.0
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-core@0.84.1-beta.0
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-server@0.84.1-beta.0

- Typing in a Markdown file that uses Windows (CRLF) line endings no longer converts the edited lines to LF.

- Editing a Markdown file that uses Windows (CRLF) line endings no longer duplicates the document or drops text.

- Error dialogs such as "Cannot open this folder" no longer hide behind other windows, the Project Navigator no longer gets stuck on "Opening…", and the app still quits while one is open.

- The desktop app no longer offers a crash report after a power loss, forced power-off or system crash stopped the computer, including on Windows.
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge@0.84.1-beta.0
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-core@0.84.1-beta.0
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-server@0.84.1-beta.0

- Local telemetry now records whether the editor ran in OK Desktop, a browser tab or an AI editor's browser pane, on server HTTP spans and logs and on opt-in frontend traces. The value leaves your machine only in a bug report you send or through OpenTelemetry export you enable.

- A browser tab left open while `ok` is upgraded now asks you to reload, and saves your edits before it does.

- Links, images, and reference definitions written with an angle-bracket destination such as `[René](</People/René.md>)` now open the path inside the brackets instead of a literal `<…>` target, and still save byte-for-byte as written.

- Cmd-click on a linked code file or extensionless file now opens it in a new app tab instead of a tab showing a 404 or an empty editor.

- A link to an existing file with no extension, such as a Makefile, now opens the file preview on click instead of only showing the link popover, and agent write results no longer report it as a missing page.

- Raw asset requests whose path contains `#`, an encoded slash, a backslash, or a `.`, `..` or empty segment now return 404 for any file. Ignored files can no longer be reached this way, and files with a backslash in their name are no longer served on macOS or Linux.

- Auditing a single file that has a same-named `.md` or `.mdx` sibling no longer reports links to existing images, files, and folders as missing.

- A `[[file.png]]` or `![[file.png]]` whose file does not exist now appears in the Problems pane and the Links panel's local files, like a missing markdown link does; an existing file, by path or by file name, does not.

- `![[file.png]]` embeds now resolve by file name anywhere in the project, including folders that hold no markdown document and names that differ only in Unicode normalization.

- `![[folder/file.png]]` embeds now show their file when the embed's letter case or Unicode normalization differs from the file's path, as `[[folder/file.png]]` links already do.

## v0.83.2: v0.83.2

**Published**: 2026-10-07

Point release over v0.83.1: the current stable plus 9 applied commit(s), isolated from the changes still soaking on main.

Applied: 95f65064f9897d283c35d66384aca30efc0f37fa, 5aba6973f1cce6b1ef19d70c74a87559b6486c58, 76fb57035ff8dcd1f05f72d7f1dd32493f7b178c, 6318cbf864844e18bf83a9457952868397a8a5b7, 7e361ded62502e4ad5b1dcf9244d79a2889962a3, 1f20cae5c25c4a6e1bbf952dba70acba93abcb6b, a9e359f9790e5a3fc97c43e0f6cb023932828a48, 7db5dae8ec649db0d9fb361bb542476b94a952e0, aac70de09be5f71cdab82708cfd9e93b62c19659

### Patch Changes

- Check for updates now tells you when this copy of OpenKnowledge can't update itself, instead of showing nothing.
- Crash reports now attach only the crash dump from the crash that prompted them. If that dump can't be added, the report says so instead of attaching a different one.
- On Windows and Linux, closing the last project window now returns to the Project Navigator instead of quitting. To close the app, use File → Exit on Windows or File → Quit on Linux.
- Overlapping projects and previews now refuse to start rather than write the same files. Close overlapping previews before opening a project, restart existing servers after updating, and restart the parent after creating a nested project.
- Full bug reports and `ok diagnose bundle` now include what the operating system recorded about the app being ended, such as memory-pressure or out-of-memory kills, hangs, and shutdowns and restarts, so unexplained exits can be diagnosed.
- Settings no longer offers the Auto sync modes before it knows the project has a Git remote. Settings and the sync menu show the Shared default sync mode when you haven't picked your own, and Settings explains that the Shared default only reaches teammates when Config sharing is Shared.
- When **Check for updates…** finds a new version but its download fails, the app now shows an error instead of staying silent, and "Checking for updates…" stays visible during the check, including in Settings.
- Stop the app and browser tabs from rewriting the file list into their disk cache on every refresh, which could add up to hundreds of gigabytes of disk writes in busy projects.
- On Windows and Linux, launching OpenKnowledge while it is already running now brings its window to the front.
- The empty editor's "From template" list now says when a very large knowledge base had too many folders to list every template, and shows its count as a minimum.

## v0.83.1: v0.83.1

**Published**: 2026-10-07

### Patch Changes

- When a folder is opened using another spelling of its path, edits are saved, links and embeds find existing files, and diagnostic bundles mask both spellings of that path.

- The relaunch notice for a downloaded update now reappears in new or reloaded windows and after Check for Updates, and the Update Ready dialog offers Quit and Restart to install it right away.

- Keep successfully deleted items out of the sidebar and close their tabs when a later deletion fails.

- Keep sidebar focus and scroll position steady when the open document appears during a background refresh, while highlighting its row and preparing it for entry when focus is elsewhere.

- Prevent delayed observations of earlier saves from incorrectly blocking newer document writes with a conflict.

- Edits and deletes made through MCP right after the server starts now reach disk immediately, instead of waiting minutes for the link index to finish building. Until it finishes, write results carry a `link-check-deferred` warning in place of link checks.

- Keep explanations visible when generated-index settings updates are rejected.

## v0.82.0: v0.82.0

**Published**: 2026-10-05

### Minor Changes

- Add Polish (polski) to the language picker. The translation is provisional; corrections are welcome via the [translation page](https://openknowledge.ai/docs/contribute/translations).

### Patch Changes

- Sandboxed iframes can no longer read the local OpenKnowledge server's API, change documents, or open collaboration or agent connections. API write requests that send JSON must now label it as JSON.

- OpenKnowledge Beta now keeps its data and credentials separate from the stable app, in `~/.ok-beta`. After updating, Beta starts fresh: settings, logs, themes, agent chat history, and user config begin empty, and you sign in again. Earlier Beta data in `~/.ok` stays there for the stable app.

- After the local server restarts, open documents save their full content to the offline cache again once they sync. Previously the cache could keep only edits made after the restart.

- Stable and Beta no longer share a project's server: the second app offers to stop the first one's server instead of attaching to it. This holds once both apps are on this release. [Details](https://openknowledge.ai/docs/reference/what-open-knowledge-writes#stable-and-beta-on-the-same-project).

- Pull-only sync now always uses your configured pull interval. Signed-out followers are no longer held to one pull every 3 minutes.

- Opening a standalone Markdown file now works in unpackaged desktop builds.
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge@0.81.1-beta.0
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-core@0.81.1-beta.0
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-server@0.81.1-beta.0

- Sync, `ok pull` and share-link branch switches now refuse a change that leaves a symlink pointing outside the repository, into private `.git` or OpenKnowledge state, at secrets such as `.env`, or anywhere uncheckable. Merges that change links need Git 2.38 or newer.

- Agent connections in a development build now explain that the build can't connect agents so it leaves your installed app's setup alone, instead of saying the feature is unavailable.

- Importing skills from a local folder on Windows now accepts absolute paths like `C:\skills`, `C:/skills`, network paths and `file:///C:/skills`, and `~` expands to your home folder.

- Symlinks can no longer expose or overwrite private `.git` or OpenKnowledge files. Docs, diagrams and attachments that link into them, or outside the project, are not opened, served, saved or duplicated, and `ok clone` and opening a shared branch in a worktree refuse such links.

- On Windows without symlink rights (no admin or Developer Mode), adding a skill to another location now creates a copy instead of failing. Converting a location to a link explains why it can't and keeps the existing copy.

- An external link no longer shows a second arrow while a collaborator's cursor sits inside it.

## v0.79.0: v0.79.0

**Published**: 2026-09-28

### Minor Changes

- Text files attached to an agent chat from outside the project, or from a browser, now travel with the message instead of being skipped, within the 700 KB attachment budget.

- In agent chats opened in the browser, hovering a GitHub pull request or issue link now shows a card with its title, state, and author, plus lines changed and merge status for pull requests.

- Claude Code and Codex chats in the Agents panel can now use a browser to open pages, click, and take screenshots once you turn on **Let agent chats use a browser** in Settings → Preferences; it needs Google Chrome and Node.js and is off by default.

### Patch Changes

- When an in-app agent stops on its own while waiting for your next message or a sign-in, the chat now explains what happened in plain language, calls out the error line when there is one, keeps the rest of the output behind Show details, and offers a new chat.

- On macOS, files and folders created right after OpenKnowledge starts are no longer missed when it runs its fallback file watcher.

- In unpackaged Electron runs, a project server that is still starting when the 20 s startup deadline passes now gets up to 160 s instead of the project failing to open, and a server that times out is stopped rather than left running.

- Uninstalling from the macOS app no longer pauses while confirming OpenKnowledge has quit.
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge@0.77.10-beta.0
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-core@0.77.10-beta.0
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-server@0.77.10-beta.0

- A remembered agent reasoning level such as `xhigh` now comes back in new agent chats when another remembered setting, like turning thinking on, is what makes it available.

- In the desktop app, you can report a problem from an agent chat's Settings menu, and the report includes that conversation, with known secrets scrubbed, unless you uncheck it.

- On Windows, typing right after a terminal is moved or resized no longer occasionally drops a character from the command.

- Edits to skill and config files made just after file watching starts are no longer missed.
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-core@0.78.1-beta.0

- On Linux, the desktop app no longer crashes when a native dialog or other system UI loads icons inside a container that grants extra capabilities, such as x11docker with `--cap-add`. The reported trigger was the folder picker.

- On Windows, stopping a project server no longer risks a native crash in its file watcher during shutdown.

_Release body unavailable for: v0.78.0-beta.8 — see the per-beta releases for those changes._

## v0.77.9: v0.77.9

- Closing the Publish to GitHub dialog now returns keyboard focus to the button that opened it.

- Menus now keep space from window edges, and the Resources and app menubar menus scroll in short windows.

## v0.77.8: v0.77.8

**Published**: 2026-09-23

### Patch Changes

- Keep Agent connections ordering stable while toggling, and keep newly enabled agents visible when clearing search or collapsing the list.

- The shared composer add menu now groups files, comments, and page mentions, with commands available in in-app agent chats.

- In unpackaged desktop runs, a project server that fails to load its OpenKnowledge packages now shows that error in the "Unable to open project" dialog instead of only an exit code. Installed apps open projects through a separate path and are unaffected.
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge@0.77.8-beta.0
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-core@0.77.8-beta.0
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-server@0.77.8-beta.0

- Restored terminal tabs now start once the terminal panel is on screen, so a restart no longer leaves shells running in a panel you cannot see or close.

- A conflict resolution that deletes the file now stays retryable when saving its state fails. The file watcher no longer misreads the server's own removal as an external delete, so it no longer clears the conflict that resolution is still working on.
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-core@0.77.8-beta.0

- When an agent goes quiet for three minutes mid-turn, the conversation says so and counts the minutes, so you can decide whether to stop it. The notice clears as soon as the agent responds again; waiting on a permission prompt does not count.

## v0.77.7: v0.77.7

**Published**: 2026-09-23

### Patch Changes

- In the agents panel, hovering a tool row now says what the tool does, alongside its raw id. Expanded tool output is capped with a fade and a Show all control; JSON arguments and results are pretty-printed and highlighted, and markdown-shaped results from non-shell tools render as markdown.

- Make renderer and Utility-process crashes diagnosable from a bug report bundle. Desktop logs now retain low-rate process memory and CPU samples, per-window liveness and lifecycle events, and the last pre-crash plus live process snapshots on each crash breadcrumb.

## v0.77.6: v0.77.6

**Published**: 2026-09-23

### Patch Changes

- Links in an agent conversation that point at a document in your project now keep their `#heading` fragment, whether written as a markdown link, a backticked path or a bare path in prose. Windows paths resolve as well.

- A message queued behind a running agent turn can now be sent right away: Send now on the queued row stops the current run and sends that message next, ahead of anything else waiting.

- In-app agents now receive the Open Knowledge project skill automatically on their first non-command message, without editor setup. Gemini receives the guidance inline. For older projects showing staged skill files in git status, open the project in the desktop app to update its ignore rules.

- Link suggestions no longer count HTML and MDX component tags, such as `<Callout>` or `<Image>`, as mentions of a page with the same name.

## v0.77.4: v0.77.4

**Published**: 2026-09-22

### Patch Changes

- The agent composer now cycles its placeholder through the two triggers it accepts, so typing `@` to mention a page and `/` to run a command are discoverable. Ask AI's example prompts now also cycle, with a fade, when reduced motion is on.

- Skills in the editor's slash menu now show what they do under their name.

- A desktop window now sends its theme preference to the native appearance once per change, instead of re-sending it whenever the colour palette or the config connection settles. When one window's appearance is changed by another, switch the affected window's own theme preference and back to restore it.

- `ok deinit`, `ok uninstall`, and the desktop uninstall flow no longer refuse to remove a project's local state over host uncertainty showing no evidence of a running server, such as an already-exited process. `ok clean` prunes a lock naming one. A live or unreadable server process still blocks both.

- Sidebar keyboard focus no longer jumps to the open document when a background file change lands, so arrow keys and shortcuts keep acting on the row you chose. Renaming the open document still moves focus, because that changes which document is active.

- `@` pickers now open with the document you are on first, ahead of the rest of the workspace. In an agent conversation the picker also lists what you already attached earlier in that chat.

- A markdown link an agent writes to a document in your project now opens that document in the app. Before, it showed as blocked or did nothing when clicked.

## v0.77.0: v0.77.0

**Published**: 2026-09-21

### Minor Changes

- Browse and search chat history in a responsive side panel while keeping existing chat tabs and session behavior. An Agents panel with no conversation now reports whether it is starting one, has no enabled agent, or could not reach your agents, and offers the matching action.

### Patch Changes

- Fix theme palette assignments unexpectedly switching between light and dark, and restore the selected appearance preference when returning to Default, following the operating system when System is selected or no preference is set.

- Opening, resuming, or retrying an in-app agent now reports "Starting" rather than "Installing" unless it is really fetching a catalog agent's adapter, and screen readers announce how the wait ends. That adapter now resolves once, not per conversation; retrying one that failed to start re-resolves only that agent.

- File tabs and terminal tabs now share one look: a filled rounded tab with matching size, text size, and alignment across light and dark themes.

- The agent settings control in the chat composer now shows the model, reasoning effort, Fast mode, and says when the agent acts without asking, instead of the model alone. The yellow dot is gone; the control names what the mode does rather than signalling it by colour.

- The Ask AI composer's attach button, prompt text and agent picker now sit on a common centre line instead of three different ones, and the tab that collapses the composer paints a solid fill in dark mode, so the composer edge it sits on no longer shows through it.

## v0.74.1: v0.74.1

**Published**: 2026-09-15

### Patch Changes

- A failed tool call in the Agents panel now says what to do next when the app can tell what went wrong: an unreachable OpenKnowledge server, a timed-out request, or a permission you denied. Other failures get no guess. Rows with error text gain a copy control.

- You can rename a past chat from the history menu in the **Agents panel**. A chat's name came from its first prompt, and the only way to change it was to double-click its tab, which does not exist for a chat you have closed. The history popover is where closed chats live, and it offered only reopen and delete.

  Each row now has a rename control that edits the name in place, the way the delete confirmation already works. Enter saves, Escape abandons the edit, and an empty name cannot be saved rather than being silently discarded. A chat that is open as a tab can be renamed too, unlike delete, which still asks you to close the tab first.

- An `@doc` chip in a sent message now opens the doc it names, and looks like a link before you hover it. Chips for folders, non-docs, and docs no longer in the project stay inert.

- A markdown document save that finishes after a newer save of the same document no longer overwrites the newer saved content on disk; the late save is skipped and logged.

- `GET /api/skills` no longer fails with a 500 when built-in skill bundles resolve to their source assets (fresh checkout or mid-build). The built-in row is now consistently listed as not ignored instead of inheriting ignore state from a build-artifact path segment.

- Wiki links and embeds written with an escaped alias separator (`[[Page\|Alias]]`, required inside tables) now resolve to a clean target, anchor, and alias instead of one ending in a stray backslash; the escape you authored stays in the file. Escape-only or whitespace targets are no longer links.

- Opening a project no longer stalls while the skills list scans plugin installs registered to other projects, and directory marketplace sources that resolve outside their marketplace root no longer contribute skills.

- Reloading with live agent threads no longer forces the agents panel open. The panel reopens at the state you left it in, and only threads that go live after the reload reveal it. Browsers and projects with nothing recorded start closed and remember from the first session after updating.

- CLI presence checks no longer let an interactive shell probe freeze the app or take over the terminal. Windows probe placement is unchanged.
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge@0.72.4-beta.0
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-core@0.72.4-beta.0
  - @inkeep/open-knowledge-server@0.72.4-beta.0

- Reconciling a document without an acknowledged base no longer concatenates it with itself: the detected disk change replaces the editor content and the prior version stays restorable from the timeline. A pre-write reconcile refused for a missing base is now tracked with its own reason, `refused-no-base`.

- Agent startup now respects package release-date policies, using an older allowed release when needed, and explains when no allowed release can be installed.

## v0.73.0-beta.2: v0.73.0-beta.2

**Published**: 2026-09-14

Delta since previous beta ([v0.73.0-beta.1](https://github.com/inkeep/open-knowledge/releases/tag/v0.73.0-beta.1)) — 1 new changeset.

### Patch Changes

- When an agent asks to run a shell command, the permission gate in the **Agents panel** now shows the command it is asking you to approve, for agents that send the command with the request (Claude Code and Codex both do). Before, the gate showed only the agent's one-line description of what it wanted to do, while the command was truncated in the row above and the full text sat in a collapsed `Input` block as JSON. Approving meant trusting a sentence the agent wrote about itself.

  The command is read from the permission request itself, so it shows even when the request arrives before the tool call it gates, and it cannot change while the gate waits for your answer. A one-line command is laid out one statement per line: a `;`, `&&` or `||` ends a line and a long pipeline continues on an indented one, without splitting inside quotes, `$( )`, backticks, `${ }`, escapes or comments. A command that already spans several lines, such as a heredoc, is shown exactly as written. A long command scrolls inside the gate rather than being cut short, and hidden characters such as bidirectional overrides or zero-width spaces are shown as `⟨U+…⟩` codes with a warning.
